links.outcome: Alert rate and acceptance rate of ML-based medication alerts in outpatient prescribing
links.effect: 28,536 alerts across 1,206,895 prescriptions (2.36% alert rate); 13,947 (48.88%) accepted; 470 intercepted errors (1.64% of alerts).
links.quote: Over the two-year study period, 1,206,895 prescriptions were ordered and a total of 28,536 alerts were triggered (alert rate: 2.36 %).

unlisted_practices: Machine-learning CDSS to intercept wrong-drug and look-alike/sound-alike medication errors

screen.reason: Evaluates the real deployment of a machine learning-based clinical decision support system (MedGuard) in an outpatient hospital setting, reporting alert rates, physician acceptance, and drug error interception.
